items.title: Police widen probe into RM4.83mil drug haul at Subang Air Base
items.summary: KUANTAN: Police are working with the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) to identify and arrest more people linked to a drug syndicate that exploited military assets. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said 13 people had been arrested so far, comprising seven RMAF officers and personnel and six civilians. He was speaking after witnessing the handover of duties between incoming Pahang police chief Datuk Mohammad Shaharul Md Osman and acting state police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob, who is also the deputy state police chief.

items.title: Fahmi: Over 40,000 bullying posts wiped from social media as MCMC ramps up crackdown
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Social media platforms have removed 40,214 bullying-related content and 55 extremely offensive content involving children following requests by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) between Jan 1 and Nov 15 this year. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the statistics on the removal of bullying-related content covered all age groups and referred to the volume of content taken down, rather than the number of criminal cases or victims involved. Fahmi was replying to a question from Datuk Siti Zailah Mohd Yusoff (PN-Rantau Panjang), who wanted to know the number of cases in 2026 involving cyberbullying, sexual exploitation and harmful content targeting children, as well as the effectiveness of the social media platform licensing framework, which came into force on Jan 1, 2025.

items.title: US signals tariffs of 18-25pct, Malaysia insists on 19pct ceiling
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will continue negotiations with the United States until the first quarter of 2027, when a final decision on tariffs relating to excess capacity under Section 301 is expected. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the US had indicated a tariff range of between 18 per cent and 25 per cent for Malaysia. He maintained that Malaysia's overall tariff rate should not exceed the 19 per cent previously agreed upon under the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade (ART).

items.title: 69,000 MSMEs voluntarily adopt e-invoicing despite exemption
items.summary: "Under Phase 4, the annual sales threshold was raised from RM1 million to RM3 million, as announced by the prime minister on Aug 30, 2026. Phase 1 began on Aug 1, 2024, involving businesses with annual sales of RM100 million and above, followed by Phase 2 on Jan 1, 2025, covering businesses with annual sales of between RM25 million and RM100 million. Phase 3 began on July 1, 2025, covering businesses with annual sales of between RM5 million and RM25 million, while Phase 4 covers businesses with annual sales of between RM3 million and RM5 million.

items.title: More commercial vehicle accidents year-to-date than whole of 2025: APAD
items.summary: KUALA LANGAT: The number of accidents involving commercial vehicles in Malaysia year-to-date has been higher than last year. Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) director general Ahmad Radhi Maarof said commercial vehicles are essential to Malaysia's economic activities as they support factories, businesses, retailers and communities nationwide. However, he noted that Malaysia is seeing a rise in accidents involving these vehicles.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore to confront social media platforms over child sex crimes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will meet its Indonesian and Singaporean counterparts in mid-December to send a strong message to social media platforms over child sexual crimes. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil told the Dewan Rakyat today that the government would not tolerate such crimes being committed through social media platforms. "Whether these platforms cooperate, we pray for the best," he said.

items.title: Malaysia must build new growth engines, reduce reliance on US demand – Liew
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs to strengthen its middle class, develop more mid-sized companies and build greater technological ownership to create new engines of growth amid shifting global economic and geopolitical dynamics. He said a larger middle class with better-paying jobs, alongside more Malaysian companies with the capabilities to scale up, would help drive economic growth and reduce dependence on individual export markets. He said greater technological ownership would provide another engine of growth, allowing Malaysian companies to build stronger capabilities and participate more meaningfully in the global technology ecosystem.

items.title: Saifuddin to brief cabinet on RMAF drug case tomorrow
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail will present a full report to the cabinet tomorrow on the drug smuggling case involving Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officers. The Home Ministry would focus on lessons from the incident, including the need to tighten security at strategic premises, he said. "Tomorrow, I believe the Home Ministry will be asked to provide a full report at the cabinet meeting.

items.title: One in four jobs, RM14.4b in value: Sabah tourism’s economic clout on display
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 26 — Sabah’s tourism industry generated RM14.4 billion last year, accounting for 12.3 per cent of the state’s economy, an increase of 5.6 per cent from the previous year. Domestic tourism consumption rose 14.2 per cent to RM13.4 billion from RM11.7 billion in 2024. Inbound tourism expenditure recorded the stronger growth, increasing 20.8 per cent to RM7.5 billion, while domestic tourism expenditure grew 6.8 per cent to RM5.9 billion.

items.title: South Korea top court upholds acquittal of ex-president Yoon on perjury charges
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korea's top court on Thursday upheld the acquittal of former President Yoon Suk-yeol on perjury charges during the insurrection trial of former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo, reported Xinhua. Yoon was indicted in December 2025 on charges of giving false testimony in the previous month during Han's trial, where the former prime minister faced charges of aiding and abetting the ringleader of the insurrection. The special counsel team, however, argued that Yoon initially had no intention of holding a formal Cabinet meeting, as he summoned only six Cabinet members and later six additional members after receiving Han's advice.

items.title: Ministry targets 10-tonne padi yield per hectare by 2030
items.summary: TASEK GELUGOR: The Agriculture and Food Security Ministry aims to increase average padi yields in the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) areas to 10 tonnes per hectare by 2030. Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the target, which ranges between seven and 10 tonnes per hectare, would be achieved through modern technology, improved fertilisation and better farming practices. He said several high-performing plots were already recording yields of between eight and nine tonnes per hectare, with a handful reaching 12 tonnes.

items.title: Govt studying age limits, age verification for online gaming platforms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is studying the possibility of imposing age restrictions and verification mechanisms on online gaming platforms to protect children and teenagers. Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil said there were currently no plans to introduce special licensing requirements for online gaming service providers, similar to those imposed on social media platforms. "Its findings will help determine whether additional safeguards or regulatory measures are needed, including possible age limits and age verification mechanisms for online gaming platforms," he said.

items.title: No compensation for businesses affected by e-invoice exemption change
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will not compensate businesses that incurred e-invoicing compliance costs before the exemption threshold was raised from RM1 million to RM3 million in annual sales. Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the government had instead introduced tax incentives to ease the compliance burden, including for businesses now exempted from implementing e-invoicing. "To help businesses reduce the burden of e-invoicing compliance costs, the government does not provide compensation but has introduced tax incentives that can be claimed by all businesses, including those exempted from implementing e-invoicing," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: From traffic lights to petrol pumps, transmission fault disrupts Sabah’s East Coast
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Nov 26 — Sabah Electricity (SE) confirmed that an incident on its electricity transmission system at 6.04am on Thursday caused a power outage affecting the East Coast. The utility company activated its operations room and deployed technical teams to restore electricity supply in stages across Sandakan, Tawau, and Lahad Datu. Checks in Sandakan showed several petrol stations congested with vehicles as other outlets were forced to cease operations due to the blackout, while motorists were advised to drive cautiously with several traffic lights out of service.

items.title: Drug syndicate smuggled 3 tonnes of meth through RMAF facilities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A drug syndicate is believed to have smuggled three tonnes of methamphetamine worth RM156 million through Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) aviation facilities in Sabah, exploiting two cells operating in Tawau and Labuan. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told the Dewan Rakyat today that the syndicate's Tawau cell had carried out seven transactions involving 1.8 tonnes of drugs worth RM93 million. Its Labuan cell conducted 14 transactions since August 2024, involving another 1.2 tonnes worth RM63 million.

items.title: SpaceX cleared to launch up to one million AI satellites
items.summary: WASHINGTON: SpaceX has received approval to launch up to one million satellites into Earth orbit to establish space-based data centres for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, German Press Agency (dpa) reported. "By moving compute capacity beyond Earth, SpaceX and the many competitors working on their own orbital data centres are meeting the moment," FCC chairman Brendan Carr said. Supporters of space-based data centres argue that they could benefit from abundant solar energy and opportunities for cooling in space.

items.title: Kelana Jaya LRT services restored after power disruption at four stations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Services along the Kelana Jaya LRT line resumed at 10.09am today after Rapid KL completed repairs to the track power supply, which had disrupted operations at four stations this morning. Rapid KL said in a statement that alternative train services and free shuttle buses introduced earlier had been withdrawn following the restoration of the power supply. Rapid KL said its technical and operations teams would continue monitoring the power supply and train services to ensure stability following the repairs.

items.title: Tesla driver pleads guilty to dangerous driving causing woman's death
items.summary: KULIM: A factory engineer pleaded guilty at the magistrate's court here today to a charge of dangerous driving that caused the death of a woman on Nov 23. N. Dinendran, 29, entered the plea after the charge was read before magistrate Nur Hamizah Mat Shah. According to the charge, Dinendran drove an electric car, a Tesla, dangerously, causing the death of Noor Lela Zainon, 39.

items.title: Malaysia strengthens access to climate financing despite COP31 pact deadlock
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's participation in the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye, has helped strengthen its access to international climate financing despite participating countries failing to reach an agreement on the Antalya Pact. He said the Malaysian delegation had actively participated in climate financing negotiations based on the country's position, which was agreed upon by the National Climate Change Action Council in July and endorsed by the Cabinet in August. "These developments are important in strengthening Malaysia's access to international climate financing," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Report: Negeri Sembilan Ruler to meet MB, senior Umno leaders today
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 26 — Negeri Sembilan’s months-long political deadlock could be resolved as early as tomorrow, with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir scheduled to hold separate meetings with Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim and senior Umno leaders this afternoon, The Star reported. Ismail’s political future is expected to feature prominently during his audience with the Ruler at Istana Hinggap in Seremban. Tuanku Muhriz is subsequently expected to meet Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, his deputy Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and other senior party leaders.

items.title: One missing MyKad, one month behind bars: Sabah man’s roti canai run goes horribly wrong
items.summary: TAWAU, Nov 26 — A man who went out to buy roti canai without carrying his MyKad ended up spending a month in prison for an immigration offence before being released Wednesday after he was confirmed to be a Malaysian. Azlanshah Mahathir, 24, was freed by the High Court after Judicial Commissioner Steve Ritikos set aside his conviction and five-month jail sentence. However, his citizenship was subsequently confirmed by the National Registration Department (NRD) following biometric fingerprint verification.

items.title: Locking out tomorrow's quantum hackers
items.summary: To counter this, Malaysia is championing two vital shields: data sovereignty and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC). Data sovereignty keeps Malaysian information housed inside local data centres under domestic jurisdiction, while PQC replaces vulnerable digital padlocks with quantum-proof mathematics. Inside a dedicated national testing sandbox, cryptographers at the Malaysia Cryptology Technology and Management Centre and CyberSecurity Malaysia are already battle-testing next-generation defences.

items.title: Malaysia rules out immediate end to fossil fuel use
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia remains committed to progressively transitioning away from fossil fuels but will not adopt an approach that calls for their immediate phase-out. "At the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), I reaffirmed Malaysia's commitment to progressively transitioning away from fossil fuels. Islahuddin also asked how the government would ensure a fair and orderly energy transition without compromising energy security, economic growth and the people's well-being.

items.title: Planning to climb Mount Kinabalu? Sabah to launch new route from Kiau to Marai-Parai on Jan 16
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 26 — A new Mount Kinabalu climbing route from Kiau to Marai-Parai will be launched on January 16, marking a significant milestone in the development of mountain tourism from the Kadamaian side. Kadamaian Assemblyman Datuk Ewon Benedick said the first phase of the new climbing route would become one of Sabah’s latest tourism attractions in conjunction with Visit Sabah 2027, while opening up greater economic opportunities for local communities. He said the development of mountain tourism from Kadamaian was among the main priorities outlined under the Kadamaian Development Master Plan 2020-2035.

items.title: Snooker centre caretaker pleads guilty to exposing daughter to injury
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A snooker centre caretaker whose one-year-old daughter died after suffering multiple injuries pleaded guilty at the Sessions Court today to exposing the child to physical injury at a motel earlier this month. After the proceedings, the woman hugged Siti Aishah, and both cried uncontrollably. The child died a day after being admitted to Penang Hospital, where medical examinations revealed injuries to her abdomen, legs, forehead and back.

items.title: PAC urges further cuts to subsidised cooking oil quota, warns oversupply risks fuelling smuggling
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) today urged Putrajaya to further reduce the monthly subsidised cooking oil quota to match actual domestic consumption, warning that excess supply leaves the RM12.138 billion programme vulnerable to smuggling and leakages. The bipartisan panel recommended that the monthly quota be capped at between 19,000 and 30,000 metric tonnes to align with consumption data. The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) and the Finance Ministry (MOF) had previously lowered the monthly quota ceiling from 60,000 to 55,000 metric tonnes in June.

items.title: Malaysia faces hurdles in enforcing transboundary haze laws
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Enforcing laws against transboundary haze pollution faces challenges, particularly when those responsible operate outside Malaysia's jurisdiction. He said proving that haze originated from a neighbouring country would require sufficient evidence, including location maps, coordinates, landownership details and information on parties operating at fire sites. Arthur said the government took transboundary haze incidents seriously and was continually reviewing measures, including the feasibility of enacting a Transboundary Haze Pollution Act.

items.title: Strong flow, high tides and heavy rain combine to breach Bukit Changgang bund in Kuala Langat
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 26 — Unusually strong water flow from Hulu Langat, combined with high tides and heavy rainfall, has been identified as among the factors contributing to a bund breach at the Bukit Changgang Flood Mitigation Project site in Kuala Langat at about 6am yesterday, resulting in flooding. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director (operations) Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the Selangor Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) recorded 95 millimetres of rainfall in the area yesterday. “The incident resulted in floodwaters overflowing into a nearby village, with affected residents relocated to a temporary relief centre (PPS) at Sekolah Kebangsaan RTB Bukit Changgang, which opened yesterday.

items.title: Johor targets RM5b in halal investments, 5,000 new companies by 2030, state assembly told
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 26 — Johor has set a target of 5,000 new companies, 4,000 skilled workers and RM5 billion in cumulative investment for the state’s halal industry by 2030, said Johor Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid. Mohd Fared was responding to a question from Ng Yak Howe (PH-Bentayan) on the number of entrepreneurs in Johor who have successfully obtained halal certification since the introduction of the Johor Halal Development Plan (PKHNJ) 2030. He said 1,298 new applications for Malaysian halal certification (SPHM) from entrepreneurs and companies in Johor had been approved since the launch of PKHNJ 2030 up to November 11.

items.title: EPF manages RM1.55 trillion in assets as of September: Finance Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Employees Provident Fund (EPF) had RM1.55 trillion in investment assets as at Sept 30, according to the Finance Ministry. The EPF's dividend payouts depend on market conditions and its ability to generate sustainable long-term returns. To sustain competitive dividend payouts, the EPF adopts a disciplined investment strategy based on Strategic Asset Allocation (SAA), spreading investments across different asset classes, sectors, geographical markets and investment mandates.

items.title: Retirement funding – how do we prepare for an aged society? [WATCH]
items.summary: Malaysia is already an ageing nation, and is expected to become an aged nation – when 14 per cent or more of the population are made up of those of 65 years and older – by 2048. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir announced that a White Paper on Malaysia's preparations to become an aged nation is expected to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat on December 2, outlining whole-of-society planning. How should we prepare for becoming an aged nation?

items.title: Teen cashier shoved, kicked after customer complains about colleague's expression
items.summary: Melaka Tengah police chief Assistant Commissioner Halim Abas said initial investigations found that the incident occurred at 9.30pm on Sunday when a female customer approached the payment counter to buy a packet of cigarettes. He said the woman took issue with the victim's colleague, who was manning the counter, and told her to smile, saying she was annoyed by her facial expression. The victim lodged a police report and sought treatment at a hospital, he said.

items.title: Malaysia cannot rely on US consumers forever, Liew Chin Tong says in call for stronger Asean middle class
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Malaysia and other Asean countries must build stronger middle-class populations with greater purchasing power to reduce their dependence on the United States as a consumer market, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said. He said higher wages and developing companies capable of scaling up would be crucial to sustaining economic growth as global production capacity continued to expand. Liew also said Malaysia should move beyond being primarily a trading nation and develop greater ownership of technology rather than simply trading goods and services.

items.title: Kelana Jaya Line resumes normal operations after repairs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Train services on the Kelana Jaya Line have returned to normal following the completion of repair works after a power supply disruption affected four stations. Alternative train and bus services deployed during the disruption have also been discontinued. However, train frequencies are still being adjusted following the restoration of services.

items.title: Jendela contractor in Sabah hit with over RM200mil in penalties
items.summary: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the amount was almost equivalent to the value of the contract awarded to the company. He said penalties imposed under Jendela Phase 1 were calculated based on the number of sites awarded to each company. "The penalties or fines imposed under Phase 1 were particularly severe for the companies as they were based on the number of sites awarded.

items.title: Nestle rolls out AI safety tech across entire truck fleet
items.summary: KUALA LANGAT: Nestle Malaysia Bhd has achieved 100 per cent GPS, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled dashcam and telematics coverage across its existing transporter fleet in an effort to enhance visibility across its transport operations. Nestle Malaysia manages around 6,500 trips covering about 900,000 kilometres every month across its primary transportation network in Malaysia and Singapore. "These efforts also support the ambitions of Malaysia's National Transport Policy 2019-2030 towards safer, more efficient and sustainable transportation," added Aranols.

items.title: ‘He is all I have left’: Sister appeals for clues to UKM student missing for five weeks
items.summary: Thirty-three-year-old Nur Fatihah Mat Daud, of Kampung Sedaka Tengah, Yan, said she only learned of the disappearance of her brother, 22-year-old Muhammad Shafik Hidayat, about three days ago through a message that went viral on the WhatsApp application. “I received a message informing me that my younger brother had not attended classes at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) for quite some time. The university also contacted me to provide an update regarding his disappearance.

items.title: Penang–Kulim as Silicon Valley, Johor as second economic capital: Deputy minister urges states to drive Malaysia’s growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Malaysia must move away from concentrating economic decision-making in Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya and give states a bigger role in driving their own growth, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said. He said the country needed a new approach to economic development, envisaging specialised regional economic centres, with Penang and Kulim serving as technology hubs, Johor becoming the country’s second economic capital and Kuching developing into a national energy hub. “Think of Johor as the second economic capital,” he said.

items.title: Sabah to get biggest share of Jendela Phase 2 sites
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sabah is set to receive the largest allocation of telecommunications infrastructure sites under the second batch of the National Digital Network (Jendela) Phase 2 project, which could begin next year. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the first batch of Phase 2 involved the development of 1,000 sites nationwide, with allocations distributed almost equally among Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak. "For the first batch of Jendela Phase 2, there are 1,000 towers and sites nationwide, with about one-third each in Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng questions MACC’s handling of KLSCAH land lease probe, RM2.1b overspending
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — DAP national adviser Lim Guan Eng has accused the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) of double standards, contrasting its swift investigation into a land lease controversy involving a ministry led by Hannah Yeoh with what he described as its lack of action over RM2.1 billion in overspending by the ministry headed by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. “Has MACC launched an immediate investigation because one ministry is led by a DAP minister, while the other can be delayed because it is headed by an Umno minister who is also the deputy prime minister?” Lim said in a statement today.

items.title: Japan's data centre boom faces growing revolt from urban residents
items.summary: KASHIWA: Until a few years ago, Susumu Goto's house in Kashiwa, northeast of Tokyo, looked out on a grassy field where neighbours played baseball and soccer. Today, a couple of 31-metre-tall (102-foot) data centres owned by Hong Kong-based asset manager PAG loom in front of it. Industry group Japan Data Center Council as well as Tokyo and several other local governments have also drawn up best-practice guidelines this year as data centres have crept ever closer to homes.

items.title: Libyan student posts RM17,000 bail in fatal Jalan Jelatek crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Libyan university student charged with reckless driving resulting in the death of a retired soldier along Jalan Jelatek here has been released on RM17,000 bail with assistance from his country's embassy. A source close to the investigation confirmed that Ali Abdul Rahman Mahmoud Elmaki, 32, posted bail yesterday. The prosecution had alternatively proposed bail of RM70,000 with two Malaysian sureties if the court decided to grant bail.

items.title: Hong Kong home prices ease in October as recovery loses steam
items.summary: HONG KONG: Hong Kong private home prices dropped 0.6 per cent in October from a month earlier, reversing a recent period of stability, data from the Rating and Valuation Department showed on Thursday. The private home price index eased in October, following revised gains of 0.2 per cent in September and 0.1 per cent in August. Prices rose 6.5 per cent in the first 10 months of this year.

items.title: Picasso among four recovered 1MDB artworks that could go on public display by year-end, National Art Gallery says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A painting attributed to Pablo Picasso is among four artworks recovered in connection with the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) financial scandal that could go on public display in Malaysia as early as the end of this year, Berita Harian reported. The National Art Gallery is preparing a special exhibition featuring works attributed to Picasso, Joan Miró, Maurice Utrillo and Balthus, offering the public a rare opportunity to see artworks recovered through international efforts to trace assets linked to the scandal. A meeting on October 21 focused on the ownership status of the recovered artworks and the next steps towards staging the exhibition.

items.title: Selangor sees rise in flood evacuees as Perak numbers dip
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood evacuees at temporary relief centres (PPS) rose in Selangor, declined slightly in Perak and remained unchanged in Sabah this morning. In SELANGOR, the number of evacuees increased to 1,456 from 414 families, compared with 958 from 281 families yesterday. In PERAK, the number of evacuees at three relief centres across three districts fell slightly to 209 from 62 families, compared with 211 from 63 families yesterday.

items.title: Selangor flood evacuees jump by 500 in a day, topping 1,400
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The number of flood evacuees housed at temporary relief centres (PPS) increased in Selangor this morning, while declining in Perak and remaining unchanged in Sabah. In SELANGOR, the number of flood evacuees rose to 1,456 from 414 families, compared with 958 from 281 families yesterday. In PERAK, the number of flood evacuees at three PPS across three districts stood at 209 from 62 families this morning, down from 211 from 63 families yesterday.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh confirms MACC summoned aide over RM1,000 KLSCAH lease
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh has confirmed that her aide has been summoned by anti-corruption investigators in connection with the renewal of a 99-year land lease for the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) at a nominal premium of RM1,000, compared with an earlier estimate of nearly RM4.67 million. In a Facebook post today, Yeoh said three Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officers had visited her office at the Federal Territories Department yesterday. The lease renewal has drawn scrutiny since Yeoh announced on November 14 that the government had approved the nominal premium, substantially below the amount previously estimated.

items.title: All aboard: Abang Jo wants cruise ships dropping anchor off Kuching
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 26 — Sarawak plans to build a cruise ship jetty with immigration and customs facilities at Tanjung Sipang, a headland on the northern tip of the Santubong Peninsula near Damai, about 30km from here. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the jetty would ease entry for cruise passengers and could attract more international visitors to Kuching and nearby destinations, including Damai. He said the state planned to develop the jetty in waters 16 metres deep near the Santubong National Park, as much of Sungai Santubong was shallow.

items.title: Sabah drug ring suspected of exploiting military facilities linked to RM156m in transactions, Parliament told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A drug syndicate suspected of exploiting military aviation facilities in Sabah is believed to have been operating for years, with police intelligence pointing to previous transactions involving three tonnes of drugs worth RM156 million, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said preliminary investigations pointed to an established criminal network whose suspected mastermind had been identified but remained at large. Speaking during Minister’s Question Time, Saifuddin said police intelligence indicated that the syndicate’s Tawau cell had carried out seven previous transactions involving 1.8 tonnes of drugs worth RM93 million.

items.title: Health minister pays tribute to donor families behind 16 transplants
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Sixteen organ transplants were successfully carried out nationwide over five days, following four organ donations after brain death. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the historic achievement involved donations at Hospital Universiti Sains Malaysia, Hospital Melaka, Hospital Shah Alam and Hospital Sultanah Aminah, Johor Bahru. Hospital Selayang and Hospital Kuala Lumpur each carried out four kidney transplants.

items.title: Transport Ministry: Malaysia weighing national mental health support programme for pilots
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Malaysia is assessing the need for a national pilot assistance programme to support pilots’ mental health and wellbeing, the Transport Ministry has said, following a parliamentary question about the potential professional repercussions of seeking help. In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, the ministry said Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) already operated a peer support programme for its employees, initially involving pilots, with professional support provided through Naluri, a mental health and wellbeing service. While Malaysia has yet to establish a nationwide programme, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) has conducted mental health awareness programmes and engaged with several airlines on the mental health and wellbeing of pilots.

items.title: Putrajaya may hold e-commerce platforms accountable for uncertified goods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The government is examining measures to address the sale of uncertified imported products via e-commerce platforms, including potential action against platforms that fail to ensure compliance with quality standards. Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said his ministry will collaborate with the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to ensure that products sold online meet established standards. Although sold at low prices, these items lack quality certification, this includes electrical goods, which are required to meet safety standards.

items.title: Govt finds ‘no strong evidence’ Malaysian-linked plantation firms caused Indonesian fires, Dewan Rakyat told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A government review has so far found no strong evidence that Malaysian-linked plantation companies were responsible for fires in Indonesia, the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES) has said. In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, the ministry said it had worked with the Plantation and Commodities Ministry to examine allegations linking Malaysian companies to the fires through their ownership, investments or operations in Indonesia. The government has yet to commit to introducing legislation to hold individuals and companies accountable for overseas operations that contribute to transboundary haze affecting Malaysia.

items.title: GPS bets on youth as coalition injects fresh blood into election slate
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 26 — The introduction of 11 new faces in Gabungan Parti Sarawak’s (GPS) candidate line-up for the 13th Sarawak State Election reflects the coalition’s efforts to rejuvenate its leadership and encourage greater participation of young professionals in politics. GPS information chief Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the inclusion of younger candidates, particularly from Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), was a positive development towards ensuring leadership continuity within the coalition. GPS yesterday announced its full line-up of 82 candidates for the Dec 12 state election, with new faces accounting for approximately 13.4 per cent of the candidates.

items.title: Fatal Johor crash now a murder probe after police uncover suspected cable theft link
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A fatal road incident in Johor is now being investigated as murder after police uncovered a suspected cable theft link following the discovery of a video circulating on Facebook. Iskandar Puteri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Radin Taha said in a statement that police received a report of the incident at 4.30am on Tuesday. “Further investigation found elements of cable theft behind the incident,” Radin Ramlan said, adding that Telekom Malaysia Johor Baru had also lodged a police report.

items.title: Najib drops final bid to revive RM1.9m suit against ex-AG Tommy Thomas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has withdrawn his final bid to revive a RM1.9 million lawsuit against former attorney general Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, ending a six-year legal battle over Thomas’ decision to prosecute him. Najib withdrew his application for leave to appeal to the Federal Court today, with his lawyer, Firoz Hussein Ahmad Jamaluddin, telling the court that his client wanted to “focus on pressing issues”, Free Malaysia Todayreported. Najib was present in court, where family members and supporters filled the public gallery.

items.title: Sarawak teacher gets 260 years’ jail, 24 strokes for sexually assaulting eight young girls
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 26 — The Sri Aman Sessions Court yesterday sentenced a 35-year-old primary school teacher in Engkilili to a total of 260 years in prison and 24 strokes of the cane for 64 charges involving physical sexual offences against eight girls aged between seven and 12. Iris further ordered the man to undergo rehabilitative counselling throughout his detention period, in accordance with Section 26 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act (SOACA) 2017. Of the 64 charges, 59 were brought under SOACA 2017, comprising 22 charges under Section 14(a), 23 charges under Section 5, and 14 charges under Section 10.

items.title: Over 436kg of drugs worth RM34.89m seized in three-month KLIA security sweep, home minister says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A three-month security operation at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) uncovered 16 drug smuggling cases involving 436.66kg of drugs worth RM34.89 million, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has said. In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, Saifuddin said the operation, conducted between August 10 and November 13, involved 100 per cent baggage and body screening of targeted flights to 10 destinations. “As a result of these inspections, 16 prohibited items were detected and 16 drug smuggling cases involving 436.66kg of drugs worth RM34.89 million were thwarted,” he said.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: 19 officers sacked, eight suspended over ‘counter setting’, ‘flying passport’ syndicates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Nineteen officers have been sacked and eight others suspended from duty over integrity breaches linked to “counter setting” and “flying passport” syndicates, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has said. In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, Saifuddin said disciplinary action had been taken against 27 officers as of November 2026, with the eight suspended officers facing charges in court. Saifuddin said the agency had consolidated the inspection and enforcement functions of six government agencies, including the Immigration Department and Royal Malaysian Customs Department, under a single chain of command.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: Pilots, flight crew to face random drug tests under KLIA security overhaul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Pilots and flight crew will be subject to random drug testing under a Cabinet-approved security overhaul aimed at preventing a recurrence of large-scale drug trafficking through Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has said. “The government, through the Home Ministry and the Transport Ministry, consistently accords the highest priority to security controls at all national entry points, particularly at Kuala Lumpur International Airport,” he said. “The action plan comprises 17 substantive recommendations formulated around three key security pillars, namely aviation security, national and border security, and physical security and protection.”
